title: Storage for Moving House: Bridge the Gap Between Homes
description: How to use storage when moving house or relocating: short-term storage between homes, removals storage, container storage and how to plan the move in and out.
cardText: Short-term storage between homes, during renovations or while relocating.
h1: Storage for moving house: bridge the gap between homes
intro: Completion dates slip, renovations overrun and new homes are sometimes smaller than the old one. Short-term storage keeps your belongings safe while you sort it out.

image.alt: A woman carrying moving boxes in a living room

highlights.title: Free to use
highlights.text: Our guides and comparisons cost nothing. You book directly with the storage provider.

highlights.title: Compare before you book
highlights.text: Check size, access, security and the full monthly cost, not just the headline price.

highlights.title: Home or business
highlights.text: Advice for personal storage, business storage and everything in between.

sections.h2: When storage helps during a move
sections.html:
• A gap between leaving your old home and getting the keys to the new one
  • Renovating or decorating before you move everything in
  • Moving abroad or into temporary accommodation
  • Downsizing and not yet ready to sell or give away furniture
  • Staging a home for sale by clearing clutter

• Self-storage unit: you (or your movers) take everything to a facility. Flexible and easy to visit.
  • Portable container storage: a container is dropped at your home, you load it, and it’s stored at a depot or kept on your driveway.
  • Removals company storage: many moving companies store your belongings in their warehouse between collection and delivery. Convenient, but you usually can’t access items until they’re delivered.

sections.h2: Plan the move in and out
sections.html:
1. Book storage as soon as you know your dates, since facilities can be busy at peak moving times
  2. Pick a size using our size guide
  3. Pack the things you’ll need first at the front of the unit
  4. Keep a list of what’s in each box
  5. Check the notice period, so you aren’t charged for an extra month after you move out

Check what’s covered at each stage: on the removal truck, in storage and in transit again. Your mover’s cover, the storage provider’s cover and your own home insurance may each cover different parts, with different limits.

faqs.q: How much notice do I need to give a storage facility?
faqs.a: It varies. Many rolling contracts ask for anything from a few days to a month’s notice. Check before you sign so you can time it with your move.

faqs.q: Can movers take my things straight to a storage unit?
faqs.a: Yes. Most removals companies will deliver to a storage facility. Make sure the unit is booked, the facility is open and your movers know the access arrangements.

faqs.q: Is it better to use a container or a storage unit when moving?
faqs.a: A container saves you a trip, as you load it at home. A storage unit is easier to visit during the rental. Compare total costs, including delivery and collection.
